source.title: Cautious optimism for deep parameterized quantum circuits
source.authors: Marie C. Kempkes; Elies Gil-Fuster; Carlos Bravo-Prieto; Aroosa Ijaz; A. Wilms; J. Eisert; E. V. van Nieuwenburg; V. Dunjko

record.tranche_reason: Tests model-size double descent in parameterized quantum circuits, extending the phenomenon to a different model family and setting.
record.gate_note: The paper sweeps circuit size and reports test-loss curves for three datasets and four training-set sizes. Training is fixed at 2500 epochs, so it does not test epoch-wise descent; varying training-set sizes does not by itself establish that more data raises error near interpolation. It also reports theoretical peaks in risk bounds, which are not measurements of the actual risk curve. Figure F.1 probes assumptions about Hessian and Jacobian spectra; those are mechanism results, not tests of the listed effective-complexity claim.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps the parameter count of gradient-trained data re-uploading quantum circuits and reports test loss across the interpolation threshold p=NK. This is model-wise double descent in a non-deep-network model class, so it bears on V4. The theoretical results concern risk bounds, not measured risk.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors also state that their main analytical result is that the risk bounds, not the risk itself, peak at interpolation. The numerics on test loss serve as empirical support. They caution that the results hold only for trainable PQCs and do not show overparameterized circuits beat underparameterized ones.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gradient-trained data re-uploading quantum circuits, test loss, and an add-one-in/random-matrix analysis rather than the original classical deep-network settings and methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported curves vary with dataset and training-set size; no epoch, noise, or regularization sweep is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Analytical lower and upper bounds on expected risk for scalar-output PQCs with Gaussian inputs attain a maximum at p=N in the proportional limit, under stated assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under spectral assumptions on the Hessian and Jacobian, PQC expected-risk bounds peak at the interpolation threshold p=N.

fits_no_version.finding: The mechanism checks on MNIST-1D (Fig. F.1) show three things. The functional-Hessian λmax falls toward interpolation, Jacobian rank saturates at NK, and the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the gradient covariance dips near p=NK.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In PQCs the interpolation peak coincides with a minimum of the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the gradient covariance (a Marčenko–Pastur soft edge).

record.problems: The numerical curves are presented graphically without tabulated values; experiments use ten repetitions and simulated circuits. The theoretical peak results concern bounds under assumptions and do not by themselves establish a peak in actual expected risk. The study tests only trainable data re-uploading PQCs and does not test epoch-wise descent or whether more data raises error near interpolation.

untested.parts: Models are parameterized quantum circuits, not deep neural networks.
Training length is fixed at 2500 epochs; no epoch-wise curve is reported.
N is varied (21–48), but no comparison is reported of test loss at fixed p across N showing that more data raises error. The figure might allow this, but the text does not state it.
Only one quantum model family (re-uploading PQCs on 8 qubits, depth-varied). Kernel or other model classes are not tested here. Concentration-dominated, untrainable regimes are excluded by design.
The peak is located at the raw count p=NK. No effective-complexity measure is tested across size, epochs and samples.
Label noise and regularization are not swept. The regression task has fixed noise sd 0.5. Multiple peaks are not examined.
No effective-parameter re-parameterization of the curve is attempted.

record.verdict_notes: The 'toy_network' subject_kind is loose for PQCs but harmless. The empirical support depends on output rescaling (c=150), which the authors say was needed for reliable convergence. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: The models tested are parameterized quantum circuits, not deep neural networks.
Training time is not swept; models are trained for 2500 epochs.
The paper varies training-set size but does not report that increasing sample size raises test error near interpolation.
Tests data re-uploading PQCs on the stated tasks, not a broad sweep across other model classes.
Does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts the peak location across size, epochs, and sample size.
Does not test peak dependence on label noise or regularization, or multiple descent peaks.
Does not compare the curve against an effective parameter count to test whether the second descent becomes an ordinary U-shape.

rows.note: The paper explicitly cautions that this bound result alone does not imply that expected risk itself has double descent.
rows.check: A theorem about a lower bound on expected risk under Assumptions 1–7, not a measured risk curve. The authors say it does not imply the risk itself shows double descent (App. C). It belongs in fits_no_version, not as an empirical row.
